evidence.quote: let isNew (r: Receivables) = r.Books.Customers.IsEmpty && r.Books.Drafts.IsEmpty && r.Books.Invoices.IsEmpty && r.Payments.IsEmpty
| Ready, Some books when not (Transfer.isNew books) ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule is in Tier 2. Summa.Storage.Transfer decides the file format, the order of refusals, the data-version check and whether books are new. Summa.Web.Engine decides the GitHub/local, files-pack and new-books outcomes and the canTransferBooks flag. The Tier 3 wire only maps kernel event names to engine messages. app/index.html restates the new-books rule only as help text and decides nothing.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect below Tier 4. The time comes in through the message context (ctx.Now) and the business date through businessToday model ctx. The download is requested as the existing OfferDownload engine effect, and the save goes through the existing save path (a SaveBooks effect). Transfer.fs is pure string and JSON work with no I/O or clock reads, so every decision can be tested without effects.

evidence.quote: { model with Error = Some "Books on GitHub are moved with their repository, not with a transfer file."; Notice = None }, []
{ model with Error = Some "Books on GitHub are moved with their repository, not with a transfer file."; Notice = None }, []

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Most new facts have one definition: Schema, Version, StampFormat, NotATransferFile, isNew and fileName, all reused by the engine. Some are restated, though the copies agree. The GitHub refusal (outcome and sentence) is written out twice in two adjacent match arms instead of once. Who may transfer is stated a second time as the view flag canTransferBooks, separately from the guards in apply. The date format 'yyyy-MM-dd' is written separately in fileName and importedNotice. None of these copies contradict each other.

evidence.quote: | BooksTransferTextChanged v -> { model with BooksTransferText = v; BooksTransferPreview = Transfer.preview v }, []

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new rules are all in Tier 2 Summa.Storage.Transfer: what the contents count, the versions accepted, the contents-mismatch refusal and the preview wording with plurals. The engine only calls Transfer.preview and the view only shows the stored value. app/index.html only binds booksTransferPreview. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code changes or decides anything.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effects. The preview is computed by pure code inside the engine transition. The export still uses the ctx.Now it was given, and no clock, I/O or port use is added.

evidence.quote: | Error why -> $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"
| Error why -> { model with Error = Some $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"; Notice = None }, []
"Books imported from a transfer file exported on " + t.ExportedAt.UtcDateTime.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "."
| Some(Json.Integer v) when v = 1L || v = int64 Version ->

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one definition (Transfer.contents), used by export, read, preview and the tests. But some facts are copied. The refusal sentence 'This file cannot be imported: …' is now written both in Transfer.preview and in the engine's BooksTransferImported branch. The export's UTC date, formatted 'yyyy-MM-dd', is computed separately in preview and importedNotice. The accepted legacy version is a bare literal 1L next to the named Version constant. All copies agree today but could drift.
